title: Stadium with a long span steel roof, Brisbane: structural steel
workplace: Stadium with three grandstands, concourses, corporate boxes and a long span steel roof, Brisbane
note: Facts are example inputs for testing. On a real project they come from the contractor's own procedures and the project's documents.

swms.title: Long span roof trusses
swms.task: Erect the long span steel roof trusses with two crawler cranes in a dual lift, landing them on temporary support towers, and bolting the connections from boom lifts more than 2 m above the ground.

facts.craneCompany: Lifts are done by the crane company under its lift plan; the crane company's dogman slings and releases loads, and our licensed dogman receives and lands them with tag lines.
facts.fallControl: Connections are bolted from boom lifts with guardrails, with harnesses attached to the boom lift anchor points. No one climbs the steel.
facts.controlsConsidered: Edge protection was considered for every task, and an elevating work platform where edge protection cannot be fixed.
facts.temporarySupport: Temporary support towers are to the engineer's design TS-12 (revision B), installed and checked by the steel erection engineer before any truss is landed on them.
facts.erectionSequence: Steel is erected to the designer's sequence on drawing SE-020 (revision D), with temporary bracing as shown, and the steel erection engineer checks the structure is stable before connections are released.

steps: Plan lifts with the crane company
Work with the crane crew during lifts
Lift and land steel with the crane company
Erect and connect steel at height
Plan and do the dual lift
